decisions.statement: The settings the akasha folder compiles under are said here alone.
A file of the akasha folder compiles against the full ESNext library.
A program built over made-up files names the library those files compile against.
A file from outside the akasha folder is parsed without the link from each node to the one above it.
A global under a name the browser also declares collides rather than replacing that declaration.
Code built for a runtime with no browser is judged without the browser.
The program reads every body through one reader handed to the program.
A file outside the akasha folder is read as the file is.
A file the akasha folder compiles is named `.ts` or `.tsx`.
The akasha folder compiles TypeScript written with JSX.
A package manifest is read through the reader the program was handed.
A placement names the folder each package's manifest sits in.
A placement is worked out from the manifests among the paths handed in.
A path through the packages folder under a placed name is answered where that manifest sits.
A path through the packages folder under an unplaced name is answered where its link leads.
A real path is worked out from the placement before the link on disk is read.
A link is followed whether or not a file is there to follow that link to.
A manifest the reader answers nothing for is read from the disk.
Nothing here judges the answers this module finds.
A body served to the program has a version.
The compiler's own library is parsed once for the life of the process.
A body the akasha folder compiles is parsed anew for each program.
Nothing here writes inside the akasha folder.

definition: a program built over the pages
